$sources: EN 1998-1:2004 Sec 3 (ground types, elastic and design spectra), Sec 4 (importance, mass, lateral force and modal analysis, torsion, drift, second order), Tables 5.1, 6.2 and 9.1 (behaviour factors), recommended values
source: EN 1998-1:2004 Sec 3, 4, 5.2.2.2, 6.3.2, 9.3 with the recommended values (National Annexes may set others)

SA.description: Ground type A: rock or rock-like formation, at most 5 m of weaker material at the surface (vs,30 > 800 m/s)

SB.description: Ground type B: very dense sand, gravel or very stiff clay (vs,30 360-800 m/s, NSPT > 50, cu > 250 kPa)

SC.description: Ground type C: dense or medium-dense sand, gravel or stiff clay (vs,30 180-360 m/s, NSPT 15-50, cu 70-250 kPa)

SD.description: Ground type D: loose-to-medium cohesionless soil or soft-to-firm cohesive soil (vs,30 < 180 m/s, NSPT < 15, cu < 70 kPa)

SE.description: Ground type E: surface alluvium of type C or D, 5-20 m thick, over material with vs > 800 m/s

rcSmf.name: RC frame system, DCH (q = 4.5 αu/α1, αu/α1 = 1.3)

rcImf.name: RC frame system, DCM (q = 3.0 αu/α1, αu/α1 = 1.3)

rcOmf.name: RC frame system, DCL (low seismicity only, q = 1.5)

rcSpecialWallFrame.name: RC uncoupled wall system, DCH (q = 4.0 αu/α1, αu/α1 = 1.1, kw = 1)

rcOrdinaryWallFrame.name: RC uncoupled wall system, DCM (q = 3.0, kw = 1)

rcSpecialBearingWall.name: RC uncoupled wall system carrying the gravity loads, DCH (q = 4.0 αu/α1, αu/α1 = 1.1, kw = 1)

rcOrdinaryBearingWall.name: RC uncoupled wall system carrying the gravity loads, DCM (q = 3.0, kw = 1)

rcDualSpecial.name: RC dual system, wall-equivalent, DCH (q = 4.5 αu/α1, αu/α1 = 1.2)

rcDualDcm.name: RC dual system, wall-equivalent, DCM (q = 3.0 αu/α1, αu/α1 = 1.2)

steelSmf.name: Steel moment resisting frame, DCH (q = 5 αu/α1, αu/α1 = 1.3)

steelScbf.name: Steel frame with concentric diagonal bracings, DCH (q = 4)

steelOcbf.name: Steel frame with concentric diagonal bracings, DCM (q = 4)

steelEbf.name: Steel frame with eccentric bracings, DCH (q = 5 αu/α1, αu/α1 = 1.2)

steelDualSmfScbf.name: Steel moment resisting frame with concentric bracing, DCH (q = 4 αu/α1, αu/α1 = 1.2)

siteSpecificStudy.warning: Ground type {classes} (flagged by the soil report): {code} {clause} asks for special studies of the seismic action on this ground (and of liquefaction, S2), and gives no spectrum for it. Until they are made, the design spectrum uses ground type {used} and the category of the seismic action uses {assumed}: an assumption, not a value of the code.

allowableDriftLabel: Buildings with brittle non-structural elements attached to the structure (dr·ν ≤ 0.005 h, ν = 0.5 for importance classes I and II, 0.4 for III and IV)

driftLimits.label: Ductile non-structural elements, or finishes designed for the drift (dr·ν ≤ 0.0075 h)

torsion.label: Torsional sensitivity indicator: drift at one end over the mean (reported)

outOfPlaneOffset.label: Lateral system not continuous to the base

soft.label: Abrupt change of the storey stiffness

mass.label: Abrupt change of the storey mass

clauses.soft: EN 1998-1 Sec 4.2.3.3(3) (SAEngine indicator: 70 % of the storey above)
clauses.mass: EN 1998-1 Sec 4.2.3.3(3) (SAEngine indicator: 150 % of an adjacent storey)

verticalComponent.members: horizontal members spanning 20 m or more, cantilevers longer than 5 m, prestressed horizontal members, beams supporting columns and base-isolated structures

spectrumTypeGuidance.text: override seismic.spectrumType; a National Annex may use both or give its own rule

sources.spectra: EN 1998-1 Tables 3.2 (Type 1) and 3.3 (Type 2), recommended values; Type 2 where the earthquakes that contribute most have Ms ≤ 5.5 (Sec 3.2.2.2(2)): override seismic.spectrumType
sources.siteClasses: EN 1998-1 Table 3.1 ground types A-E: SAEngine keeps the site class ids SA-SE (the soil report classes the ground by the same vs,30, NSPT and cu limits)
sources.designSpectrum: EN 1998-1 Sec 3.2.2.5, Eqs 3.13-3.16, β = 0.2 recommended (3.2.2.5(5)); ag = γI·agR (3.2.1(3)), the settings' Z is agR in g
sources.lateralForce: EN 1998-1 Sec 4.3.3.2.2(1) Eq 4.5: λ = 0.85 if T1 ≤ 2·TC and more than two storeys; Sec 4.3.3.2.3(3) Eq 4.11 with the linear mode shape
sources.periodCoefficients: EN 1998-1 Sec 4.3.3.2.2(3) Eq 4.6: T1 = Ct·H^(3/4), Ct 0.085 steel moment frames, 0.075 RC moment frames and steel eccentric bracings, 0.050 others
sources.systems: EN 1998-1 Table 5.1 (q0 of RC systems), 5.2.2.2(5) (αu/α1), (11) (kw = 1 for frame and frame-equivalent systems, walls with hw/lw ≥ 2 assumed), Table 6.2 (steel), Table 9.1 (masonry, the lower recommended values); R stands for q, Cd for qd = q (4.3.4(1)), Ω0 for αu/α1 (SAEngine practice: EN 1998-1 has no Ω0)
sources.designCategories: SAEngine practice: EN 1998-1 has no Seismic Design Category. The zones of zoneCoefficients are bands of agR; category B: very low seismicity (ag·S ≤ 0.05 g, Sec 3.2.1(5)), C: low seismicity (ag·S ≤ 0.10 g, Sec 3.2.1(4), DCL permitted), D: otherwise (DCM or DCH)
sources.requiredDetailing: EN 1998-1 Sec 5.3.1 and 3.2.1(4): DCL only in low seismicity; else DCM (intermediate) at least
sources.allowableDrift: EN 1998-1 Sec 4.4.3.2(1)a and (2): dr·ν ≤ 0.005 h with ν = 0.5 (classes I, II) and 0.4 (III, IV), recommended
sources.driftLimits: EN 1998-1 Sec 4.4.3.2(1)b: dr·ν ≤ 0.0075 h with ductile non-structural elements; (1)c 0.010 h with no interfering elements is not offered (override seismic.allowableDrift)
sources.driftAmplification: EN 1998-1 Sec 4.3.4(1) Eq 4.23: ds = qd·de, qd = q
sources.stability: EN 1998-1 Sec 4.4.2.2(2)-(4) Eq 4.28: θ = Ptot·dr/(Vtot·h); θ ≤ 0.10 no second order effects; 0.1 < θ ≤ 0.2 by 1/(1 - θ); θ ≤ 0.3
sources.liveShare: EN 1998-1 Sec 3.2.4(2) Eq 3.17 and 4.2.4 Table 4.2: ψE = φ·ψ2 with ψ2 = 0.3 (EN 1990 Table A1.1, categories A and B) and φ = 1.0 (SAEngine takes the roof's and the largest value: storeys may take 0.5-0.8, override seismic.liveShare)
sources.heavyLiveLimit: SAEngine practice: imposed loads above 5.0 kN/m² taken as category E (storage), ψ2 = 0.8, φ = 1.0
sources.partitionWeight: EN 1991-1-1 Sec 6.3.1.2(8): the movable partition allowance is an imposed load, so it counts with ψE
sources.minimumScale: EN 1998-1 has no lower bound of the modal base shear relative to the lateral force method: no scaling
sources.massParticipation: EN 1998-1 Sec 4.3.3.3.1(3): modes with at least 90 % of the total mass (and every mode over 5 %)
sources.torsionIrregular: SAEngine practice: EN 1998-1 Sec 4.2.3.2 judges plan regularity by the torsional radius (rx ≥ ls, e0 ≤ 0.30 r), not by the drift ratio; the 1.2 / 1.4 drift ratios are reported only
sources.torsionAmplificationMax: EN 1998-1 has no torsional amplification Ax: 1.0, no amplification (Sec 4.3.3.2.4's δ is torsionalEffects)
sources.verticalFactor: EN 1998-1 Sec 4.3.3.5.2: not a fixed share of a_h; the vertical component is verticalComponent
sources.dynamicAnalysis: EN 1998-1 Sec 4.3.3.2.1(2): the lateral force method needs T1 ≤ 4·TC and ≤ 2.0 s and regularity in elevation
sources.separation: EN 1998-1 Sec 4.4.2.7(2)-(3): SRSS of the peak displacements; 0.7 where the floors are at the same elevations
sources.dampingCorrection: EN 1998-1 Sec 3.2.2.2(3) Eq 3.6: η = √(10/(5 + ξ)) ≥ 0.55 (elastic spectrum only; the design spectrum has the damping in q)
sources.siteSpecificStudy: EN 1998-1 Sec 3.1.2(4): ground types S1 and S2 need special studies
sources.irregularities: SAEngine practice: the checks of the analysis that tell about EN 1998-1 4.2.3.3 (continuity of the lateral systems; the storey stiffness at least 70 % of the storey above and the mass at most 150 % of an adjacent one as indicators of an abrupt change: the code gives no numbers); the drift ratio of the ends is reported only
sources.regularity: EN 1998-1 Sec 4.2.3.2(4) Note (λ = Lmax/Lmin <= 4), (5) (the floor within its convex envelope: the area between at most 5 % of the floor's), (6) Eqs 4.1a-4.1b, 4.2 (e0 <= 0.30 r, r >= ls), (8) (the stiffness centre and r from the moments of inertia of the vertical elements: the approximate definition for buildings that meet its conditions); 4.2.3.3(2) (lateral systems continuous to the top), (5) Figure 4.1 (setbacks: symmetric each <= 20 % of the dimension below, a single one in the lower 15 % of the height <= 50 %, unsymmetric each <= 10 % and together <= 30 % of the base's); 4.2.3.1(7) (not regular in elevation: q0 × 0.8), 5.2.2.2(6) (not regular in plan: αu/α1 the mean of 1.0 and the system's), Table 4.1 (models and methods); SAEngine practice: the centre of mass at the floor's centroid, a setback symmetric when its two sides differ by at most 25 % of it
sources.torsionalEffects: EN 1998-1 Sec 4.3.3.2.4(1) Eq 4.12 (δ = 1 + 0.6 x/Le), (2) (1.2 x/Le for planar models): applied where the analysis has no accidental eccentricity cases (4.3.2(1), 4.3.3.3.3 otherwise); SAEngine practice: the centre of mass at the plan's centre, the larger of the two directions' δ, rounded up to 0.05
sources.modalCombination: EN 1998-1 Sec 4.3.3.3.2(1)-(3): modes i, j independent when Tj <= 0.9 Ti; SRSS where every pair is independent, else CQC (all the analysis's modes compared, on the safe side)
sources.verticalComponent: EN 1998-1 Sec 4.3.3.5.2(1) (only where avg > 0.25 g, for the members listed), Table 3.4 (avg/ag 0.90 Type 1, 0.45 Type 2), 3.2.2.5(4)-(5) (vertical design spectrum, plateau 3.0 avg/q with q <= 1.5), 4.3.3.5.2(4) Eqs 4.22 (0.30 combination); SAEngine practice: the plateau value (short vertical periods) and every member (on the safe side)
sources.foundationCapacity: EN 1998-1 Sec 4.4.2.6(2) Eq 4.30 (EFd = EF,G + γRd Ω EF,E), (2) Note (γRd = 1.0 for q <= 3, 1.2 otherwise), (3)-(4) (Ω = Rdi/Edi <= q); SAEngine practice: Ω = q (the elastic response, the bound 4.4.2.6(2) allows), overridable by seismic.foundationCapacity.omega
sources.spectrumTypeGuidance: EN 1998-1 Sec 3.2.2.2(2) Note 1: Type 2 where the earthquakes that contribute most to the hazard have Ms <= 5.5 (recommended)

clauses.sdc: EN 1998-1 Sec 3.2.1(4)-(5) (SAEngine's category of the seismic action)
clauses.irregularity: EN 1998-1 Sec 4.2.3 (regularity criteria; the drift ratio reported only)
